correctness.rationale: Killed-interval Brownian resolvent gives p_safe=1-cosh z/cosh2z and E active=(1-sech2z)/r; regenerative equation m=E active+p_safe(delta+m) yields exact formula for arbitrary independent finite-mean wait. r=0 exit Dirichlet problem gives L²/(2D). For d=1/18 the positive-factor-cleared difference has vanishing x² and x⁴ Taylor coefficients and strictly positive coefficients at all orders n>=3, proving strict global no-benefit at and above the threshold; below it the x² expansion is negative and coercivity ensures an optimal positive rate. A separate finite-difference backward equation agrees at 40 parameter pairs, and exact-rational tests check coefficients; the infinite theorem rests on the symbolic sign proof.

value.rationale: Grange established winding-speedup in a zero-cost shortest-arc return model, but actual restarting typically has refractory downtime. The one-ninth exact boundary is a physically meaningful, dimensionless feasibility test, not a routine one-off numerical substitution: it is necessary and sufficient for any rate, treats equality strictly, is universal over an entire class of independent waiting distributions, and requires a global analytic sign argument. It gives a negative impossibility result for all rates as well as existence below the threshold, without claiming optimizing-rate uniqueness.
